newsitem.title: FRANCE: KLM targets French cargo for Abidjan route.
newsitem.headline: KLM targets French cargo for Abidjan route.

text.p: KLM Cargo said France-originating goods were likely to account for the majority of freight carried on a new twice-weekly Boeing 767 passenger service between Amsterdam and Abidjan, capital of the Ivory Coast in West Africa, to be launched end-March 1997.

"West Africa is a big market for French products and we expect they will account fo between 60 and 70 percent of freight carried on the Schiphol-Abidjan service, a Paris-based KLM Cargo official told Reuters
Palletised belly capacity on the 767 works out at around ten tonnes of palletised freight, the official said.
"Abidjan is something of a prime cargo route from Paris, attracting a very good level of rates and we definitely see some scope to develop off-line traffic from France."
Northbound shipments would largely be in the form of perishables, notably fish, the official added.
Air France operates a once to twice weekly full-freighter service between Paris and Abidjan as well as a daily Airbus 310 passenger service.
Pan-African carrier, Air Afrique, also operates a daily passenger service on the route. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
